newsitem.title: UK: Signet rebels threaten meeting - paper.
newsitem.headline: Signet rebels threaten meeting - paper.

text.p: Rebel shareholders in Signet Group Plc are threatening to call an emergency meeting to force the jewellery chain to reorganise its complex capital structure, which includes nine classes of share capital, the Daily Telegraph said on Saturday.
The threat came a day after Signet was thrown into disarray when talks to sell its H. Samuel and Ernest Jones jewellry chains collapsed.
The proceeds of the sale, thought to be about 280 million stg, were to have been used to reduce Signet's debts of 360 million stg, the Telegraph said.

The paper quoted James Rubin, a partner in the U.S. investment management group Sass, Lamle, Rubin and Co, which owns Signet ordinary and preference shares, as saying: "We believe the company has been deficient in reorganising its share structure."

Signet finance director Walker Boyd told the paper: "We are continuing to examine our options. We do need to achieve a fiancial restructuring and we will talk to shareholders about it." Signet trades in the U.S as Sterling.
